physiology:
The traditions place this code's seat in the thymus, the small, almost forgotten gland tucked behind the breastbone in the middle of the chest. It is the gland that teaches the immune system what belongs and what does not, a quiet inner instructor that decides, cell by cell, what to let in and what to defend against. It is fitting for a code that turns on the difference between taking and giving, between defending the small self and opening the chest to a wider room.

The shadow has its bodily floor here. Pride lives in the chest, behind a held breath, behind a sternum that has stopped softening. When the strategy of the ledger runs, the chest tightens, the breath gets shallow, the body keeps a low guard up even in friendly company. There is a watchfulness that does not rest. The thymus, under that kind of long alertness, dims down.

The climb out is also bodily, and it begins as warmth. A softening behind the breastbone. The breath going deeper than it has gone in a while. A wish to be in a room with other people again, not strategically, just because they are there. The chest learns it can stay open and still be safe, and the gland behind it answers in kind. Cleverness in service of the room runs lighter through the body than cleverness in service of the self.
amino_acid:
Deeper still, this code answers to a single amino acid, Threonine. Threonine is one of the small set the body cannot make for itself. It has to be taken in from outside, carried across the line of the mouth, broken down, and only then put to use in the building of new tissue and the holding together of skin and gut.

There is a teaching in that, and it is a quiet correction to the shadow's whole story. The code most haunted by the fear of not enough runs on a chemistry that has never been self-supplied. Even the body that is so clever at taking is, at its base, a receiver. Nothing here was ever made alone. The thing that lets the cleverness become artful, that lets the pride become invisible, is this old chemical fact running under the floorboards. The body has been being given to, all along, by the world it thought it had to outwit.
